headline: Orphaned Gorilla Thrives in the Wild, Becomes a Mother
meta_description: Lulingu, a Grauer's gorilla rescued from illegal wildlife trade as a baby, has given birth to her first infant after being returned to the wild in 2024.
summary_short: A Grauer's gorilla named Lulingu, rescued from illegal wildlife trafficking as an 18-month-old orphan, has successfully given birth to her first baby in the wild.
body:
A Grauer's gorilla named Lulingu has given birth to her first baby, marking a remarkable milestone in her journey from captivity to motherhood in the wild.

Lulingu was rescued from the illegal wildlife trade when she was just 18 months old. After years of rehabilitation, she was returned to her natural habitat in 2024. Her successful pregnancy and birth demonstrate both her own resilience and the potential for orphaned wildlife to thrive when given a second chance.

The birth represents a quiet victory for conservation efforts aimed at protecting Grauer's gorillas, one of the world's most endangered subspecies. Lulingu's story shows that rescue and rehabilitation can work—that an animal stolen from the forest as an infant can heal, grow, and contribute to the survival of her species.
quick_facts: Rescued as an 18-month-old orphan from illegal wildlife trade
Now a mother to her first baby in the wild
